correctness.rationale: For all m>=2, tightness on n=2m-1 gives 2m integer factorial moment identities. For r<m, a squared node polynomial makes these identities inconsistent with positive Gaussian measure. For r=m, the monic node polynomial is uniquely determined by a positive-definite rational Hankel system, so all radii squared are distinct algebraic; Vandermonde inversion makes all radial quadrature weights algebraic. Equal external sample weights imply e^(xi-xj) equals a ratio of products of integers and algebraic weights, contradicting Hermite-Lindemann for distinct algebraic xi,xj. Positive m-node Laguerre quadrature plus (n+1)-th root angular cancellation gives an explicit strictly positive weighted Parseval construction. Checker 106 exact finite assertions verifies supplementary identities, not all-degree proof.

value.rationale: The Gaussian quadrature m-shell baseline is natural for exact Fock moments up to degree 2m-1. The theorem separates equal-coefficient from arbitrary-positive-weight measurement designs by a strict extra-radius necessity in every odd degree, irrespective of angular oversampling; the weighted m-radius construction is exact. This is a structural obstruction with natural signal-sampling motivation, not an arbitrary parameter slice or numerical increment. No claim that m+1 equal-weight radii suffice.
